conditions: Keep the change inside the leased RPC source file; no shared Kernel/f13/job helper mutation or permission expansion.

Immediately after newJob and before launchWithCallback, set and query JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION on the same owned Job. Require exact expected flags and values; at minimum reject both breakaway flags. Preserve KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE.
Any Set/Query/readback mismatch fails before child resume, closes the original Job/pipes and allows no fallback, adaptive higher limit or automatic retry.
Keep existing timeout, cancellation, cleanup and Root outer scope bounds. These new fields do not impose CPU, disk, network or cumulative process-count limits.

A pinned sidecar may record only observed configured limits: same Job/run identity, requested and queried fields, timing before launch/resume, source hash and actual registered test receipt. It cannot mint Native qualification or model permission.
Before claiming observation, review implemented source and actual controlled fake Job readback. No such budget implementation/test observation exists in this proposal review.
semantics: 16 counts simultaneously active associated processes, including root and descendants, not cumulative process creations.

1 GiB and 2 GiB cap per-process and Job committed virtual memory, respectively; they are not RSS or a bound on all machine/kernel resources. Allocation exceeding commit limits can fail; do not describe the settings as guaranteed immediate whole-Job termination.
Values are accepted as conservative initial caps, not measured capacity. Native/tool preparation may fail under them; that remains a failed consumed attempt, not permission to increase or replay.

source_read.observation: newJob currently applies only KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE. launchWithCallback atomically assigns the Job at suspended process creation and invokes the callback before ResumeThread.
